s1.syndrome_frame: Gradually enlarging, pruritic, erythematous skin lesion
salient_findings: No improvement with topical corticosteroids and antifungals
Band-like vascular proliferation in the upper dermis
key_facts: Male patient in his early 70s
2-year history of the skin lesion
Lesion located on the proximal portion of the left calf
Mildly pruritic
Erythematous and gradually enlarging
No identifiable cause for the lesion
Topical corticosteroids and antifungals applied for 2 months with no improvement
Physical examination revealed an atrophic appearance
Histopathology showed round vascular spaces lined by a single layer of endothelial cells
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD34 and CD31, negative for D2-40

shortlist.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: matches clinical presentation of a gradually enlarging, pruritic, erythematous skin lesion

shortlist.label: angioma
shortlist.why_kept: histopathology shows round vascular spaces lined by a single layer of endothelial cells

shortlist.label: pyogenic granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: rapidly growing, erythematous lesion with vascular proliferation

shortlist.label: bacillary angiomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: similar histopathological features, including vascular proliferation

shortlist.label: epithelioid hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: matches immunohistochemistry profile, including positivity for CD34 and CD31

raw.rationale: The histopathology showing band-like vascular proliferation in the upper dermis with round vascular spaces lined by a single layer of endothelial cells, and immunohistochemistry positive for CD34 and CD31, is consistent with epithelioid hemangioma.

rejected.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
rejected.why: Typically has a more prominent spindle cell component and often involves the deeper dermis

rejected.label: angioma
rejected.why: Too broad a term and does not specifically match the histopathological findings

rejected.label: pyogenic granuloma
rejected.why: Usually has a more lobular architecture and prominent inflammatory infiltrate

rejected.label: bacillary angiomatosis
rejected.why: Typically has a more prominent neutrophilic infiltrate and is associated with Bartonella infection
